verses.zh: 先知门徒对以利沙说：「看哪，我们同你所住的地方过于窄小，
verses.en: Some of the prophets[NOTE:1] said to Elisha, “Look, the place where we meet with you[NOTE:2] is too cramped[NOTE:3] for us.
notes: Heb “the sons of the prophets.”
Heb “sit before you.”
Heb “narrow, tight.”
verses.commentary: 6:1 "the sons of the prophets" See full note at 2 Kgs. 2:3.

verses.zh: 求你容我们往约旦河去，各人从那里取一根木料建造房屋居住。」他说：「你们去吧！」
verses.en: Let’s go to the Jordan. Each of us will get a log from there, and we will build a meeting place for ourselves there.” He said, “Go.”
verses.commentary:
6:2 The meeting place or communal living place was too small for their number. As a group they went to the
lowland forest near the Jordan River to harvest beams of wood for construction.

verses.zh: 有一人说：「求你与仆人同去。」回答说：「我可以去。」
verses.en: One of them said, “Please come along with your servants.” He replied, “All right, I’ll come.”

verses.zh: 于是以利沙与他们同去。到了约旦河，就砍伐树木。
verses.en: So he went with them. When they arrived at the Jordan, they started cutting down trees.

verses.zh: 有一人砍树的时候，斧头掉在水里，他就呼叫说：「哀哉！我主啊，这斧子是借的。」
verses.en: As one of them was felling a tree, the ax head[NOTE:1] dropped into the water. He shouted, “Oh no,[NOTE:2] my master! It was borrowed!”
notes: Heb “iron.”
Or “ah.”
verses.commentary:
6:5 While chopping down a beam, one of the sons of the prophets lost the head of his borrowed axe.

▣ "it was borrowed" This is the VERB (BDB 981, KB 1371, Qal PASSIVE
PARTICIPLE) which usually means "to ask" or "to beg," but in this rare context, it connotes "borrow" (i.e., strongly
request something to use).

verses.zh: 神人问说：「掉在哪里了？」他将那地方指给以利沙看。以利沙砍了一根木头，抛在水里，斧头就漂上来了。
verses.en: The prophet[NOTE:1] asked, “Where did it drop in?” When he showed him the spot, Elisha[NOTE:2] cut off a branch, threw it in at that spot, and made the ax head float.
notes: Heb “man of God” (also in v. 9).
Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
6:6 It is possible

- that Elisha put a wooden pole in the water and caught the axe head on the piece of wood (Peshitta). The
VERB (BDB 897, KB 1012, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw)
basically means "to overflow" (i.e., Deut. 11:4; Lam. 3:54). Only here is it translated "float."

- this miracle is similar to the cleansing of

- Exod. 15:23-26 (a tree used to cleanse water)

- 2 Kgs. 2:15-22 (some salt to purify a spring)

- 2 Kgs. 4:38-41 (some meal to purify stew)

verses.zh: 以利沙说：「拿起来吧！」那人就伸手拿起来了。
verses.en: He said, “Lift it out.” So he reached out his hand and grabbed it.

verses.zh: 亚兰王与以色列人争战，和他的臣仆商议说：「我要在某处某处安营。」
verses.en: Now the king of Syria was at war with Israel. He consulted his advisers, who said, “Invade[NOTE:1] at such and such[NOTE:2] a place.”
notes: The verb form used here is difficult to analyze. On the basis of the form נְחִתִּים (nekhittim) in v. 9 from the root נָחַת (nakhat), it is probably best to emend the verb to תִּנְחְתוּ (tinkhetu; a Qal imperfect form from the same root). The verb נָחַת in at least two other instances carries the nuance “go down, descend” in a military context. For a defense of this view, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 72.
The advisers would have mentioned a specific location, but the details are not significant to the narrator’s purpose, so he simply paraphrases here.
verses.commentary:
6:8-14 This paragraph describes the frustration the king of Syria had in trying to attack the king of Israel.
Every time he set an ambush, the king of Israel did not show up.

The king of Syria thought there was an Israeli spy in his inner circle! But they respond that it was
not one of them but the prophet Elisha.

It is humorous to me that the king of Syria thought he could take the prophet, who continually
warned the king of Israel, by a secret night raid!

6:8

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"shall be my camp"

TEV, JPSOA, LXX
"encamp"

NJB, REB
"attack"

Peshitta
"lie in wait"

The MT has "my camp" but the UBS Text Project, p. 340, gives it only a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

The NET Bible, p. 601, suggests an emendation that follows the NJB and REB.

verses.zh: 神人打发人去见以色列王，说：「你要谨慎，不要从某处经过，因为亚兰人从那里下来了。」
verses.en: But the prophet sent this message to the king of Israel, “Make sure you don’t pass through this place because Syria is invading there.”

verses.zh: 以色列王差人去窥探神人所告诉所警戒他去的地方，就防备未受其害，不止一两次。
verses.en: So the king of Israel sent a message to the place the prophet had pointed out, warning it[NOTE:1] to be on its guard. This happened on several occasions.[NOTE:2]
notes: The vav + perfect here indicates action contemporary with the preceding main verb (“sent”). See IBHS 533-34 §32.2.3e.
Heb “and the king of Israel sent to the place about which the man of God spoke to him, and he warned it and he guarded himself there, not once and not twice.”
verses.commentary: 6:10 "more than once or twice" The king of Syria had attempted many times to ambush the king of Israel.

verses.zh: 亚兰王因这事心里惊疑，召了臣仆来，对他们说：「我们这里有谁帮助以色列王，你们不指给我吗？」
verses.en: This made the king of Syria upset.[NOTE:1] So he summoned his advisers[NOTE:2] and said to them, “One of us must be helping the king of Israel.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the heart of the king of Syria was stirred up over this thing.”
Heb “servants.”
Heb “Will you not tell me who among us [is] for the king of Israel?” The sarcastic rhetorical question expresses the king’s suspicion.
verses.commentary:
6:11

NASB, NKJV, REB, Peshitta
"which of us"

NRSV, JPSOA
"who among us"

TEV
"which one of you"

NJB
"which of you"

LXX
"who"

NEB
"who has betrayed us"

The NASB follows the MT. The UBS Text Project, p. 341, gives this reading a "B" rating (some doubt).

verses.zh: 有一个臣仆说：「我主，我王！无人帮助他，只有以色列中的先知以利沙，将王在卧房所说的话告诉以色列王了。」
verses.en: One of his advisers said, “No, my master, O king. The prophet Elisha who lives in Israel keeps telling the king of Israel the things you say in your bedroom.”

verses.zh: 王说：「你们去探他在哪里，我好打发人去捉拿他。」有人告诉王说：「他在多坍。」
verses.en: The king[NOTE:1] ordered, “Go, find out where he is, so I can send some men to capture him.”[NOTE:2] The king was told, “He is in Dothan.”
notes: Heb “he” (also a second time in this verse); the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Go and see where he [is] so I can send and take him.”
verses.commentary: 6:13 "Dothan" This small village was located on a low hill about 10-12 miles north of Samaria.

verses.zh: 王就打发车马和大军往那里去，夜间到了，围困那城。
verses.en: So he sent horses and chariots there, along with a good-sized army.[NOTE:1] They arrived during the night and surrounded the city.
notes: Heb “heavy force.”

verses.zh: 神人的仆人清早起来出去，看见车马军兵围困了城。仆人对神人说：「哀哉！我主啊，我们怎样行才好呢？」
verses.en: The prophet’s[NOTE:1] attendant got up early in the morning. When he went outside there was an army surrounding the city, along with horses and chariots. He said to Elisha,[NOTE:2] “Oh no, my master! What will we do?”
notes: Heb “man of God’s.”
Heb “his young servant said to him.”
verses.commentary:
6:15 "the attendant of the man of God" This would have been a new servant because Gehazi had leprosy
(2 Kgs. 5:20-27).

Elisha had been an attendant to Elijah (i.e., 2 Kgs. 3:11).

▣ "Alas, my master! What shall we do?" The Syrian army had surrounded the village by night to
capture one man!

verses.zh: 神人说：「不要惧怕！与我们同在的比与他们同在的更多。」
verses.en: He replied, “Don’t be afraid, for our side outnumbers them.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”
verses.commentary:
6:16-17 I just love this text! Wow, how many times we as believers face circumstances and evil intentions
with "fear"! Elisha prays that YHWH will open the attendant's spiritual eyes that he might see the spiritual realm (notice
Gen. 21:19; 32:1-2; and Num. 22:31; also note Ps. 37:7; 91). Elisha had seen these very things in 2 Kgs. 2:10-11.
I think what happened in 2 Kgs. 7:6 is related to these spiritual armies of the Lord of hosts. Our wonderful hymn
"Open My Eyes" comes from this text.

There is one passage where opening one's spiritual eyes is a disaster (i.e., Gen. 3:5,7)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

verses.zh: 以利沙祷告说：「耶和华啊，求你开这少年人的眼目，使他能看见。」耶和华开他的眼目，他就看见满山有火车火马围绕以利沙。
verses.en: Then Elisha prayed, “O Lord, open his eyes so he can see.” The Lord opened the servant’s eyes, and he saw that[NOTE:1] the hill was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
notes: Heb “and he saw, and look.”

verses.zh: 敌人下到以利沙那里，以利沙祷告耶和华说：「求你使这些人的眼目昏迷。」耶和华就照以利沙的话，使他们的眼目昏迷。
verses.en: As the army approached him,[NOTE:1] Elisha prayed to the Lord, “Strike these people[NOTE:2] with blindness.”[NOTE:3] The Lord[NOTE:4] struck them with blindness as Elisha requested.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “and they came down to him.”
Or “this nation,” perhaps emphasizing the strength of the Syrian army.
On the basis of the Akkadian etymology of the word, M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 74) translate “blinding light.” HALOT 761 s.v. סַנְוֵרִים suggests the glosses “dazzling, deception.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “according to the word of Elisha.”
verses.commentary:
6:18 There is irony here. The attendant's eyes are opened but the Syrian army's eyes are closed.
YHWH is the provider of both (v. 20).

The NOUN "blindness" (BDB 703, KB 760) is used here (twice) and also Gen. 18:11.

verses.zh: 以利沙对他们说：「这不是那道，也不是那城；你们跟我去，我必领你们到所寻找的人那里。」于是领他们到了撒马利亚。
verses.en: Then Elisha said to them, “This is not the right road or city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you’re looking for.” He led them to Samaria.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
verses.commentary: 6:19 YHWH not only sent blindness but also confusion.

verses.zh: 他们进了撒马利亚，以利沙祷告说：「耶和华啊，求你开这些人的眼目，使他们能看见。」耶和华开他们的眼目，他们就看见了，不料，是在撒马利亚的城中。
verses.en: When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said, “O Lord, open their eyes, so they can see.” The Lord opened their eyes, and they saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they saw, and look, [they were] in the middle of Samaria.”

verses.zh: 以色列王见了他们，就问以利沙说：「我父啊，我可以击杀他们吗？」
verses.en: When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, “Should I strike them down,[NOTE:1] my master?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Should I strike them down? I will strike them down.” In the Hebrew text the first person imperfect form is repeated; the first form has the interrogative he prefixed to it; the second does not. It is likely that the second form should be omitted as dittographic or that the first should be emended to an infinitive absolute.
Heb “my father.” The king addresses the prophet in this way to indicate his respect. See 2 Kgs 2:12.
verses.commentary:
6:21-23 The king of Israel and Elisha had drastically different ideas of what to do with these captured soldiers.

Elisha's plan caused the tension between these two neighboring countries to cease for a period.

6:21 "My father" This was a title of respect and acknowledgment of leadership

- of a priest ‒ Jdgs. 17:10; 18:19

- of a king ‒ 1 Sam. 24:11

- of a servant of his lord ‒ 2 Kgs. 2:12; 5:13

- of a prophet ‒ 2 Kgs. 2:12; 5:13; 6:21; 13:14

- of a teacher ‒ Pro. 1:8; 4:1,3

- of a governor ‒ Isa. 22:20-21

It was most often used of a parent or of YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHER

verses.zh: 回答说：「不可击杀他们！就是你用刀用弓掳来的，岂可击杀他们吗（或译：也不可击杀，何况这些人呢）？当在他们面前设摆饮食，使他们吃喝回到他们的主人那里。」
verses.en: He replied, “Do not strike them down! You did not capture them with your sword or bow, so what gives you the right to strike them down?[NOTE:1] Give them some food and water, so they can eat and drink and then go back to their master.”
notes: Heb “Are [they] ones you captured with your sword or your bow (that) you can strike (them) down?”
verses.commentary: 6:22 "with sword and bow" This was an idiom for the use of any kind of weapon in warfare.

verses.zh: 王就为他们预备了许多食物；他们吃喝完了，打发他们回到他们主人那里。从此，亚兰军不再犯以色列境了。
verses.en: So he threw a big banquet[NOTE:1] for them and they ate and drank. Then he sent them back[NOTE:2] to their master. After that no Syrian raiding parties again invaded the land of Israel.
notes: Or “held a great feast.”
Heb “they went back.”

verses.zh: 此后，亚兰王便・哈达聚集他的全军，上来围困撒马利亚。
verses.en: Later King Ben Hadad of Syria assembled his entire army and attacked[NOTE:1] and besieged Samaria.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “went up.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
verses.commentary:
6:24 "Ben-hadad" This is the first time in this context that a king of Israel or Syria is named. It is still hard to date
these events because there were two known kings of Syria by this name at this time. It meant "son of Hadad,"
a royal title.

verses.zh: 于是撒马利亚被围困，有饥荒，甚至一个驴头值银八十舍客勒，二升鸽子粪值银五舍客勒。
verses.en: Samaria’s food supply ran out.[NOTE:1] They laid siege to it so long that[NOTE:2] a donkey’s head was selling for eighty shekels of silver[NOTE:3] and a quarter of a kab[NOTE:4] of dove’s droppings[NOTE:5] for five shekels of silver.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “and there was a great famine in Samaria.”
Heb “and look, [they] were besieging it until.”
Heb “eighty, silver.” The unit of measurement is omitted.
A kab was a unit of dry measure, equivalent to approximately 2 quarts (2 liters).

The consonantal text (Kethib) reads “dove dung” (חֲרֵייוֹנִים, khareyonim), while the marginal reading (Qere) has “discharge” (דִּבְיוֹנִים, divyonim). Based on evidence from Akkadian, M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 79) suggest that “dove’s dung” was a popular name for the inedible husks of seeds.
Heb “five, silver.” The unit of measurement is omitted.
verses.commentary:
6:25 "famine" A besieged city had several problems.

- no food

- no water

- rampant disease

In the paragraph this terrible situation is characterized as

- the high cost of a poor piece of meat (even an unclean and unusual piece of meat)

- the high cost of cooking fuel (dung)

- the JPSOA's footnote says it refers to "carob pods" (Akkadian), which were normally not eaten by humans

- Roland deVauz, Ancient Israel, p. 200 calls it "wild onions"

- during sieges humans even ate dung and drank urine (cf. Isa. 36:12)

- the cannibalism (vv. 28-29)

For a good brief discussion of "siege warfare," see Roland DeVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 236-238.

verses.zh: 一日，以色列王在城上经过，有一个妇人向他呼叫说：「我主，我王啊！求你帮助。」
verses.en: While the king of Israel was passing by on the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Help us, my master, O king!”

verses.zh: 王说：「耶和华不帮助你，我从何处帮助你？是从禾场，是从酒榨呢？」
verses.en: He replied, “No, let the Lord help you. How can I help you? The threshing floor and winepress are empty.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “From where can I help you, from the threshing floor or the winepress?” The rhetorical question expresses the king’s frustration. He has no grain or wine to give to the masses.

verses.zh: 王问妇人说：「你有甚么苦处？」她回答说：「这妇人对我说：『将你的儿子取来，我们今日可以吃，明日可以吃我的儿子。』
verses.en: Then the king asked her, “What’s your problem?” She answered, “This woman said to me, ‘Hand over your son; we’ll eat him today and then eat my son tomorrow.’

verses.zh: 我们就煮了我的儿子吃了。次日我对她说：『要将你的儿子取来，我们可以吃。』她却将她的儿子藏起来了。」
verses.en: So we boiled my son and ate him. Then I said to her the next day, ‘Hand over your son and we’ll eat him.’ But she hid her son!”

verses.zh: 王听见妇人的话，就撕裂衣服；（王在城上经过）百姓看见王贴身穿着麻衣。
verses.en: When the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes. As he was passing by on the wall, the people could see he was wearing sackcloth under his clothes.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the people saw, and look, [there was] sackcloth against his skin underneath.”
verses.commentary:
6:30 "tore his clothes. . .sackcloth" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES.

verses.zh: 王说：「我今日若容沙法的儿子以利沙的头仍在他项上，愿　神重重地降罚与我！」
verses.en: Then he said, “May God judge me severely[NOTE:1] if Elisha son of Shaphat still has his head by the end of the day!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “So may God do to me, and so may he add.”
Heb “if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on him today.”
verses.commentary:
6:31 "May God do so to me and more also, if. . ." This was an oath formula (i.e., Ruth 1:17; 1 Kgs. 19:2; 20:10).

The king of Israel blamed Elisha for the siege and the problems connected to it.

verses.zh: 那时，以利沙正坐在家中，长老也与他同坐。王打发一个伺候他的人去；他还没有到，以利沙对长老说：「你们看这凶手之子，打发人来斩我的头；你们看着使者来到，就关上门，用门将他推出去。在他后头不是有他主人脚步的响声吗？」
verses.en: Now Elisha was sitting in his house with the community leaders.[NOTE:1] The king[NOTE:2] sent a messenger on ahead, but before he arrived,[NOTE:3] Elisha[NOTE:4] said to the leaders,[NOTE:5] “Do you realize this assassin intends to cut off my head?[NOTE:6] Look, when the messenger arrives, shut the door and lean against it. His master will certainly be right behind him.”[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “and the elders were sitting with him.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “sent a man from before him, before the messenger came to him.”
Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “elders.”
Heb “Do you see that this son of an assassin has sent to remove my head?”
Heb “Is not the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?”
verses.commentary:
6:32 "a man from his presence" This person is called "the messenger" in v. 32, twice and once in v. 33.
When verse 33 says "he said," it must refer to this messenger.

The exact meaning of the message from the king is difficult to understand. The king is attributing
the problem to YHWH. The king implies he has waited for YHWH to act, but no more.

2 Kings 7:1-2 should go with chapter 6. Chapters 6-7 form a literary unit.

▣ "this son of a murderer" This is an idiom not directed at the parents but at the king of Israel himself.

BDB 119 uses "son" as a member of a group (i.e., 1 Sam. 20:30).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "SONS OF. . ."

verses.zh: 正说话的时候，使者来到，王也到了，说：「这灾祸是从耶和华那里来的，我何必再仰望耶和华呢？」
verses.en: He was still talking to them when[NOTE:1] the messenger approached[NOTE:2] and said, “Look, the Lord is responsible for this disaster![NOTE:3] Why should I continue to wait for the Lord to help?”
notes: The Hebrew text also has “look” here.
Heb “came down to him.”
Heb “Look, this is a disaster from the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
6:33 AB, p. 80, along with other commentaries, thinks the person speaking in v. 33 is not the messenger of
the king, but the king himself. Probably the messenger sent to assassinate Elisha came with the king right behind him.

Josephus (Antiq. 9.4.4) states that the king had changed his mind about killing Elisha and
hurried to the meeting to stop his messenger!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What was the purpose of the miracle of vv. 1-7?

- What is the significance of v. 17?

- Explain the pronouns of vv. 32-33 (esp. the "he" of v. 33).

interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 6:1-7

1Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Behold now, the place before you where
we are living is too limited for us. 2Please let us go to the Jordan and each of us take
from there a beam, and let us make a place there for ourselves where we may live." So he said, "Go."
3Then one said, "Please be willing to go with your servants." And he answered, "I shall
go." 4So he went with them; and when they came to the Jordan, they cut down trees.
5But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water; and he cried out and
said, "Alas, my master! For it was borrowed." 6Then the man of God said, "Where did
it fall?" And when he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there, and made the iron
float. 7He said, "Take it up for yourself." So he put out his hand and took it.
